site.description: Hao Yu, PhD researcher in Engineering at Cambridge. Vapour-phase synthesis of low-dimensional materials, Raman/PL spectroscopy and Python analysis. Thesis submitted 30 September 2026.

records.title: Materials growth, understood through measurement.
text: I study how precursor chemistry and confined vapour transport shape low-dimensional materials. My work connects close-space growth experiments with Raman and photoluminescence spectroscopy, collaborative characterisation, and Python analysis.

records.title: Thesis submitted
text: PhD researcher in Engineering at the University of Cambridge. Thesis submitted on 30 September 2026.

records.title: Research profile
text: I am a PhD researcher in the Hofmann Group at Cambridge, working on tungsten oxides and transition-metal dichalcogenides. My doctoral research examines how source chemistry, source–substrate geometry and processing conditions influence material formation.

My approach combines controlled growth experiments with quantitative Raman/PL analysis and complementary evidence from collaborators. I also develop RamanPL_2D to turn spectroscopy datasets into fitted parameters, spatial maps and structured outputs.
Earlier work at Oxford connected photonic-device measurements with design and simulation. Alongside research, I have experience in technology assessment and deep-tech commercialisation.

records.title: Vapour-phase synthesis
text: Close-space sublimation and oxide-to-sulphide conversion: relating precursor chemistry and confined transport to the morphology of low-dimensional materials.

records.title: Spectroscopy and characterisation
text: Raman/PL measurements and spatial mapping, interpreted alongside collaborative structural and chemical characterisation to connect processing with material response.

records.title: Research software and analysis
text: Python workflows for preprocessing, peak fitting, mapping and batch export of spectroscopy data, developed around experimental materials questions.

records.title: Close-space growth of tungsten oxide and sulphide nanostructures
text: How does a confined vapour geometry influence oxide and sulphide nanostructure formation?

I designed and conducted CSS-facilitated CVD growth and Raman/PL measurements, and co-wrote the first-author paper with Stephan Hofmann. The study connects precursor delivery and growth conditions with material formation.
Operando SEM, TEM/EDX and XPS measurements in this study were performed by collaborators.

records.title: NaCl-assisted close-space growth of WS₂
text: How can source treatment and source–substrate geometry guide planar WS₂ growth?
I investigated salt-assisted close-space growth using paired source–substrate analysis and Raman/PL measurements to examine precursor evolution alongside deposition outcomes.
This work forms part of my submitted thesis; a first-author manuscript is in preparation.

records.title: Optical characterisation of directly written MoS₂
text: How can spectroscopy assess the layer structure and optical response of directly written 2D material?

I contributed Raman and photoluminescence measurements and analysis to a collaborative closed-loop crystal-layer writing study. The growth platform and complementary measurements were led by other co-authors.
The co-authored manuscript is under review.

records.title: RamanPL_2D
text: From raw spectra to fitted parameters and spatial maps.
I developed a Python toolkit for Raman and photoluminescence preprocessing, peak fitting, spatial mapping, batch workflows and metadata-aware export.
The software provides reusable analysis workflows for experimental spectroscopy datasets.

records.title: Photonic resonance trimming
text: Earlier research · University of Oxford
My MEng research concerned micro-ring resonator tuning. I contributed measurements, design and simulations to the subsequent Nano Letters paper on photonic-resonance trimming.
This work connects my materials background with photonic-device analysis.
